reviews.text: The clues in ‘Murder Mystery 2’ are clever and inclusive, like the music at the ‘sangeet’ for a jolly travelogue pulled along smoothly on the rails of Aniston’s and Sandler’s considerable comic talent
reviews.author: Mini Anthikad-Chhibber

reviews.text: While Murder Mystery 2 might lack depth and a concrete theme to balance the narrative, Aniston and Sandler make it an undeniable delight worth watching.
reviews.author: Gissane Sophia

reviews.text: Sandler and Aniston have such a breezy chemistry that we wish that this entire series had the kind of smarts and creativity to be found in the Knives Out films and TV's The AfterParty
reviews.author: Erik Childress

reviews.text: Not bad but not great either. Some fun moments but not enough to count.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: It is the sort of amiable entertainment that can prove quite entertaining, but not particularly so, and it probably only bears being enjoyed once.
reviews.author: Grant Watson

reviews.text: Murder Mystery 2 ends up being only moderately enjoyable.
reviews.author: Jake Peffer

reviews.text: It’s definitely not a cinematic masterpiece, but Murder Mystery 2 delivers enough silly chuckles to be worth a watch.
reviews.author: Sameen Amer

reviews.text: It’s a Friday night movie; one to watch with a glass of something and the brain in sleep mode.
reviews.author: Stephen Romei

reviews.text: Yeah, it’s not brilliant, but like recent Adam Sandler Netflix comedies, it’s just trying to entertain, and it manages to do so.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: The screenplay gives Nick and Audrey more tiresome bickering than sparkling banter.
reviews.author: Margot Harrison

reviews.text: Like a warm bath for your frontal lobes.
reviews.author: Michael Talbot-Haynes

reviews.text: Murder Mystery 2 doesn’t pack the same surprises as its predecessor. There’s not as much novelty in seeing Jennifer Aniston and Adam Sandler banter back and forth as married private investigators, but it proves nearly as fun.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Lyles

reviews.text: "Murder Mystery 2" is simple, generic and completely idiotic. Adam Sandler and Jenifer Aniston are there less for their acting skills and more to connect with the viewer because they are familiar and loved. It's an exercise of disposable entertainment.
reviews.author: Shawn Edwards

reviews.text: Absolutely unbearable. A phoned-in and uninspired vanity project.
reviews.author: Lael Loewenstein

reviews.text: It just doesn't work. Bad jokes that fall flat.
reviews.author: Wade Major

reviews.text: I can’t say the first one did much for me; the same applies to this film. Even saying it’s an amusing romp that doesn’t require much attention feels like too much praise to award to a movie so uninterested in doing more with what it has.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: But fans of the first film and/or the ensemble cast will enjoy this sequel, which keeps a brisk pace and successfully hits more comedic beats than its predecessor.
reviews.author: Jennifer Green

reviews.text: Fans of Sandler and Aniston will enjoy this movie which does not require you to have seen the original to enjoy it. Murder Mystery 2 is not remotely as bad as the first, but it still is not all that great.
reviews.author: Alex Maidy

reviews.text: Jeremy Garelick’s direction is dull and unexciting and, paired with bad CGI and green screen locations, Murder Mystery 2 is one of the worst films we’ll see this year.
reviews.author: Maria Lattila

reviews.text: Inferior to the first, functional film in every single way. With such a clueless script and second-rate production, we are the victims of this cinematographic crime. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Nestor Bentancor

reviews.text: This is an option to consider if you want a disposable pastime that doesn't make you think too hard. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mikel Zorrilla

reviews.text: Aniston and Sandler are better than this material, and it’s such a shame that this sequel couldn’t even muster up mediocre.
reviews.author: Natasha Alvar

reviews.text: ...a sporadically watchable yet predominantly forgettable comedy that is, for the most part, foiled by its exhaustingly slick and generic sensibilities...
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: Pyrotechnics are plentiful, but laughs are not.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: A silly & formulaic low-stakes whodunnit that wastes its talented cast. The writing perpetuates the stereotype of dumb Americans, so it’s baffling that Aniston + Sandler don’t take offense to that.
reviews.author: Ruth Maramis

reviews.text: Ding-dongs solving mysteries is a decent premise. But the house style of the movies is more celebrities-delivering-lines rather than its two leads committing to the camp of it all.
reviews.author: Nina Metz

reviews.text: The plot is fairly unguessable and the stunts aren’t bad, but everyone involved could surely have tried harder.
reviews.author: Edward Porter

reviews.text: These characters could have made for a broader puzzle, but the real point of this movie is to distract you for an hour and some change.
reviews.author: Alci Rengifo

reviews.text: Whodunnits are supposed to be a mix of tension and escapism, but this one tries to throw in a dose of comedy, and wavers between those tones like a rusty seesaw.
reviews.author: Asher Luberto

reviews.text: Sandler is an incredibly likeable on-screen presence, despite (or maybe even because of) the way he barely seems to be trying.
reviews.author: Alex Hudson

reviews.text: Something of a trifle, Murder Mystery 2 at least actually succeeds at entertaining and manages some solid, pleasant looking photography — perhaps not a tremendous feat, but a bit more than the majority of Hollywood blockbusters manage these days.
reviews.author: M.G. Mailloux

reviews.text: Murder Mystery 2 just went bigger but forgot the fact it’s supposed to be a whodunit and not just a wild European caper.
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: Where the first film had a surprising amount of character, this feels cobbled together by an algorithm, purely to please established fans. It may break streaming records for Netflix again, but I doubt anybody's going to be talking about it afterwards.
reviews.author: Alistair Ryder

reviews.text: This crime caper has a certain frenzied energy, but it’s sloppily plotted, crass and so dumb, you wouldn’t trust it to use cutlery unsupervised.
reviews.author: Wendy Ide

reviews.text: ...too contrived to feel real, yet not quite over-the-top enough to be hilarious.
reviews.author: Luke Y. Thompson

reviews.text: Murder Mystery' 2's  script is ok for the most part, but nothing one wouldn't expect from a murder mystery.
reviews.author: Allison Rose

reviews.text: Murder Mystery 2 isn’t a perfect sequel. It excels on new fronts while scaling back on others; a whiplash of excitement and disappointment. But it goes bigger and better in many areas, which is all you could ask for.
reviews.author: Sara Clements

reviews.text: It is what it is.
reviews.author: Joanna Langfield

reviews.text: Murder Mystery 2 changes course, switching to more of an action couple’s comedy like Date Night, and some much-needed improvements are made. Though, fewer risks are taken, and an outcome you easily see coming from a mile away.
reviews.author: M.N. Miller

reviews.text: Millions of Netflix subscribers would probably watch this movie even if it were merely mediocre. But the cast and crew don’t coast on that.
reviews.author: Noel Murray

reviews.text: Have we really reached the point where we’ll watch pretty much anything that’s put in front of us at home?
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: Neither the murder nor the mystery in Murder Mystery 2 is of any note, but the film commits in other ways. The throwaway comedy bits actually land this time around.
reviews.author: Bilge Ebiri

reviews.text: …even if Murder Mystery 2 feels like a lazy option for both audiences and cast, it works the familiar action/comedy formula to reasonably satisfying effect….
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: The makers steadfastly go for it in a fast-paced and thrilling adventure ride that leaves us waiting for the next one.
reviews.author: Ronak Kotecha

reviews.text: Here we are with a sequel that surpasses the sluggish proceedings of the original (though the bar wasn’t set high in the first place), but with the same quality of vapid proceedings that don’t leave a trace.
reviews.author: Shikhar Verma

reviews.text: Really the details of how all this fits together don’t really matter. The fun is watching Sandler and Aniston get large paychecks for looking like they are having a grand old time.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: As Murder Mystery 2 flops toward the finish line, you might look at your watch and gasp at the realization that several minutes still remain.
reviews.author: Chris Vognar

reviews.text: Murder Mystery 2 is nothing more than Adam Sandler and company in “let’s make a movie while vacationing” mode
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: Murder Mystery 2 answers the question “What could be more disposable than Murder Mystery?"
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: The story is painfully lackluster, the characters are completely undeveloped, and a lot of the humor falls flat.
reviews.author: Chris Joyce

reviews.text: Like its predecessor, Murder Mystery 2 is built on old-fashioned star power and the interplay between Sandler and Aniston. They’re good company to be in, and sometimes that’s enough.
reviews.author: Jake Coyle

reviews.text: They might be mucking around like they’re at a murder mystery dinner party, but they’re all so uniformly talented that it’s still entertaining to watch.
reviews.author: Clarisse Loughrey

reviews.text: If you’re bored this Friday evening and “unobjectionable” feels like enough of a recommendation, Murder Mystery 2 is ready and waiting.
reviews.author: Liz Shannon Miller

reviews.text: It boils down to Sandler and Jennifer Anitston having a blast. This is a quick and often hilarious slice of crime solving hijinx.
reviews.author: Leo Brady

reviews.text: Better than the original. Jennifer Aniston and Adam Sandler continue to be the main reason to watch these films. Their chemistry and charming banter complement a more action-oriented story this time around. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: The film is designed for and tailored to fit them [Sandler and Aniston]. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pablo O. Scholz

reviews.text: Unfortunately... it's just plain boring. And, frankly, there isn't a whole bunch of "murder" in this mystery.
reviews.author: Callum Crumlish

reviews.text: ... This is just another vehicle for Sandler to do his well-oiled schtick with his pals, directed with a near-obstinate lack of imagination.
reviews.author: John Nugent

reviews.text: Some predictable storylines and some frustrating rehash make it impossible to call this an improvement. Still, for a Friday night watch, you can do a lot worse.
reviews.author: Alan French

reviews.text: Perhaps the lamest element of all is the actual detective work, for which blame falls on a screenplay that cheats itself silly, devising nonsensical ways to bring characters back from the dead, then taunting us with their bogus ingenuity.
reviews.author: Tim Robey

reviews.text: Aniston and Sandler do a lot by merely relying on their familiarity with one another as performers.
reviews.author: Brian Tallerico

reviews.text: The unrelenting, unapologetic mediocrity of Murder Mystery continues with this sequel.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: ... It's principal merit is to last less than 90 minutes. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ezequiel Boetti

reviews.text: Despite its limitations, Murder Mystery is a sequel that surpasses low expectations... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Juan Pablo Russo

reviews.text: Lucky that Aniston and Sandler's magic to make us laugh no matter what is still intact. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Janire Zurbano

reviews.text: The playful patter between Sandler and Aniston makes it go down easily. It ain't much, but at least it's something.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: Low-hanging fruit is fine, but Sandler is eminently capable of pushing his comedic work to something edgier or more sophisticated...I know he’s got it in him to do a genuinely killer comedy.
reviews.author: Jeff York

reviews.text: If the Murder Mystery series swerves further and further from its original premise, it’s still got the whodunit at heart: A big cast coming together to get along and have fun. It’s undeniably infectious.
reviews.author: Dom Sinacola

reviews.text: The good news? It’s only a meager 93 minutes.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: Leans even more into comedy and the current trend of billionaire fantasyland settings, rather than good old-fashioned mystery. Like its lazy title, “Murder Mystery 2” settles for the lowest version of itself.
reviews.author: Marya E. Gates

reviews.text: There’s no doubt the cast is having a good time. Unfortunately the fun they seem to be having doesn’t exactly carry over to us.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: That the clumsiness of the characters extends to the film itself makes Murder Mystery 2 a sequel which is not only inferior in its construction, but in how it doesn’t take advantage of its talented leading duo who are left roaming with nowhere to go.
reviews.author: Chase Hutchinson

reviews.text: Murder Mystery 2 is just really fun despite its hiccups. Adam Sandler and Jennifer Aniston are a comedic duo you can believe have been married for 16 years.
reviews.author: Kate Sánchez

reviews.text: The real mystery is why they made a second one.
reviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski

reviews.text: If one is wanting something substantive, with big laughs and surprising twists, Murder Mystery 2 should be avoided at all costs.
reviews.author: Ferdosa Abdi

reviews.text: Ever since Knives Out snapped the whodunit back to wicked life, it’s harder to accept a lazy, dim-witted mystery that wastes Sandler and Aniston on 89 minutes of sequel piffle. One of those new AI bots could have coughed up a script with more personality.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: Adam Sandler and Jennifer Aniston work so well-together as a married couple as their decades-long real-life friendship comes forth on screen. The chemistry is effortless in how they play off each other.
reviews.author: Paul McGuire Grimes

reviews.text: I don't precisely understand what the villain's motivation was... What's more important is that I was never, ever having a bad time as the movie — under 90 minutes — played out.
reviews.author: Jordan Hoffman

reviews.text: Has the benefit of being short, but it doesn’t improve on the previous movie, content to basically do the same thing, only with more body-bashing encounters to explore.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: By the time it starts having some actual fun and arriving at something close to a point, the movie is well past the halfway mark.
reviews.author: Andrew Parker

reviews.text: If you squint especially hard and hold your breath till you pass out, the sequel almost resembles an attempt by Sandler to recreate Glass Onion.
reviews.author: Barry Hertz

reviews.text: A relatively low-stakes film that gets by on the charm of its two lead performers.
reviews.author: Josh Spiegel

reviews.text: The “Murder Mystery” films aren’t great mysteries, but they don’t have to be. They’re good enough.
reviews.author: Owen Gleiberman

reviews.text: Leans heavily on strained gags and physical slapstick that mostly don’t land, unless you find such things as business cards equipped with dental floss inherently funny.
reviews.author: Frank Scheck

reviews.text: It’s made just-about-watchable by Sandler and Aniston again, whose combined movie star charm proves magnetic enough to carry us through the flatter moments...
reviews.author: Benjamin Lee

reviews.text: You could do worse for something to turn on while making dinner.
reviews.author: Brandon Yu

reviews.text: Dismally lazy nonsense whose only redeeming element is that its credits roll a good 10 minutes before the conclusion of its stated runtime.
reviews.author: Nick Schager

reviews.text: The humor feels forced, and the mystery isn’t as engaging. In true sequel fashion, they even managed to leave the ending of this one open for a third installment.
reviews.author: Amanda Guarragi

reviews.text: I'd much rather see an interesting, outlandish bad movie than a totally forgettable, average one. Sadly, Murder Mystery 2 is the latter.
reviews.author: Charlie Ridgely

reviews.text: While we could criticise it for being a simple, untaxing piece of fluff, that's actually what recommends it. It's one of those movies where you can sit back, relax and let it wash over you – and celebrate the daftness of it all while you do.
reviews.author: Jo Berry

reviews.text: [Supposed] to be a self-aware celebration of the whodunnit genre. But unfortunately, just like with the first one, the sequel [isn't that ...] Murder Mystery 2 ... is just pure cringe, somehow always finding itself on the wrong side of the tracks.
reviews.author: Akhil Arora

reviews.text: “Murder Mystery 2” is a beautiful travelogue whodunit laced with corny jokes.
reviews.author: Russ Simmons

reviews.text: ... This film belongs to Sandler and Aniston and, more precisely, to their considerable comedic talents. It would be a feeble business without them, but they keep it watchable throughout.
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: Murder Mystery is now Adam Sandler's funniest franchise since he never revisited Billy Madison, Happy Gilmore or the Zohan.
reviews.author: Fred Topel

synopsis: Now full-time detectives struggling to get their private eye agency off the ground, Nick and Audrey Spitz find themselves at the center of an international abduction when their friend the Maharaja is kidnapped at his own lavish wedding.
